stack.tokenFormat: W3C Design Tokens (DTCG) 2025.10: 10 *.tokens.json files behind a resolver with sets foundation and semantic and one modifier, theme (light default, dark)

parts.summary: Roles are named by purpose in kebab-case in both themes, and DESIGN.md (Overview: Reading the tokens) documents one mapping from id to class and variable, enforced by the contract check and the token-classes lint.
The token tiers hold, but code outside the lint's reach states colours no token holds: a drifted hand copy of primary-text in the CV PDF template and a 50% on-surface tint in the Tailwind template.
The tokens parse as DTCG 2025.10 through Terrazzo, both themes define the same 24 roles, and both stylesheets are built by Terrazzo behind a --check staleness gate and an edit-denying hook.
DESIGN.md explains every role and has a reading guide, but its prose restates token values (durations, container widths, blur) and component sizes that also live in code.

findings.title: The CV PDF template hand-copies primary-text as #007C5A, which no longer matches the token (#007856), and hand-picks three more colours

evidence.excerpt: /** DESIGN.md `primary-text`: the one colour in the document. */

findings.why: A hand copy of a token value is a second source, and this one has already drifted from palette.mint-11 (principles 1 and 4; profile Pitfalls, Hand copies). The design ESLint rules only cover src/ and .storybook/, so nothing catches it.
findings.fix: Read the resolved light values at generation time (add @terrazzo/plugin-js to terrazzo.config.ts and import color.primary-text, color.on-surface, color.on-surface-variant, color.outline from the generated tokens.js), then extend design/no-raw-color to scripts/generation.

findings.title: The shimmer-text utility makes a 50% tint of on-surface that no token holds

evidence.excerpt: code never reads the palette, and never makes a colour by opacity: a new

findings.why: A role mixed with transparent is an opacity tint. No document knows it, and DESIGN.md's own rule says a new tint is a derived role (principles 4). The ESLint design rules do not read CSS, so no gate sees it.
findings.fix: Add a derived role for the shimmer's faded ink (a mix rule under $extensions.cv-screener.derived, in both themes) and use var(--color-<role>) in the gradient, or record in DESIGN.md why this gradient stop is exempt.

findings.title: The components contract leaves out components the code has: the empty-state headline and frame, the progress line and the candidate name

evidence.excerpt: root: "inline-flex max-w-full flex-col items-start text-label-lg text-on-surface",

findings.why: The contract is the component tier: a component missing from it has roles that no check ties to it (principles 2). Lowered from error to warning because every entry in the contract names a role, and the prose (Components: Empty state, Progress line, Answer views) names these components' roles.
findings.fix: Add contract entries (for example empty-state-headline, empty-state-frame, progress-line, candidate-name) that name the roles and text styles the prose already gives them.

findings.title: DESIGN.md prose restates token values and component sizes that the tokens or the code also hold

`primary` hairlines (1px in light, 0.5px in dark, where mint on near-black
character 75ms apart, the full question held 1.5s, deleted at 30ms a

findings.why: A value written in the rules document and again in tokens or code is two sources that drift (principles 1). The prose states the values of motion.duration-color-mode-turn, containers.question, containers.preview, motion.duration-medium/short, motion.blur-out-of-focus and motion.duration-focus-move instead of citing their ids, and repeats sizes that DESIGN.md itself says live in code (line 397). The contract check covers only the front matter, so this is a review item.
findings.fix: Cite the token ids where a token exists (for example `motion.duration-color-mode-turn`, `containers.question`), and name the code constant instead of its number for component-owned sizes and timings (Button.recipe.ts, typewriter.ts, theme.template.css).

findings.title: 20 of the 24 light colour roles have no $description
findings.why: The description travels with the token into every tool (DTCG Format 5.2.1). Only the four derived roles carry one here, and those four state their rules.
findings.fix: Give each role a one-line $description of its use, taken from DESIGN.md, Colors, and turn on Terrazzo core/descriptions for the role groups.

findings.title: 20 of the 24 dark colour roles have no $description
findings.why: The description travels with the token into every tool (DTCG Format 5.2.1).
findings.fix: Add the same $description as the light role, since a role keeps its meaning in every theme.

findings.title: A comment in globals.css cites colors.surface and colors.on-surface, but the token ids are color.surface and color.on-surface
findings.why: A renamed id has to be translated by every reader (decisions, Naming). Lowered to info because only a comment is affected: the code reads var(--color-surface) correctly.

gates.does: Resolves both themes with @terrazzo/parser and fails when a palette entry is an alias, a role neither points to the palette nor carries a derived rule, a derived value differs from what its rule gives, the themes' roles or rules differ, or a text style's family or weight is a literal. It reads the rule from $extensions.cv-screener.derived, which is why the plugin's check-tokens.mjs flagged primary-hover, primary-pressed, surface-panel and on-surface-subtle as literals.

tool.name: scripts/design-tokens/tokenSource.ts via npm run design:export and npm run design:lint

gates.does: Terrazzo parses the resolver and every token file against DTCG 2025.10 and runs its recommended validation rules; a parse or validation error fails the build

tool.name: tz build (Terrazzo 2.7.1), inside npm run design:export

gates.does: Fails a token or group name that is not kebab-case

tool.name: Terrazzo core/consistent-naming: set lint.rules to { ...RECOMMENDED_CONFIG, "core/consistent-naming": ["error", { format: "kebab-case" }] } in terrazzo.config.ts

gates.does: Reports a colour role or derived token without $description

tool.name: Terrazzo core/descriptions with ignore for palette.*, font.*, motion.*, breakpoints.*, containers.*

gates.does: Fails front matter keys other than version, name, description, imports and components; an imports path other than the resolver; and a contract entry that states a value, reads the palette or names an unknown token. The @google/design.md linter then checks references and contrast in both themes. It does not yet check backticked ids in the prose, or that every component in src/components has a contract entry.

tool.name: scripts/design-tokens/designDocument.ts (contractProblems) and @google/design.md lint, via npm run design:export and npm run design:lint; extend with prose-id resolution and component coverage

gates.does: Fails a class that names no token, an arbitrary value, a modifier on a token utility, a palette variable, and a hex or literal colour function in source. It covers only src/**/*.{ts,tsx} and .storybook/**/*.tsx, not CSS files or scripts/generation.

tool.name: ESLint design/token-classes and design/no-raw-color (scripts/design-lint/rules), strict in lint:strict; widen the files to scripts/generation and add a CSS check for colour functions over roles in src/styles/theme.template.css

gates.does: Builds into a temporary folder and fails when tokens.generated.css or theme.generated.css differs from the committed file; the agent's PreToolUse hook denies an edit to either
Runs lint:strict, design:export -- --check and design:lint on every push, so a commit made with --no-verify or without the hooks installed still fails

tool.name: CI workflow running the existing npm scripts (CI=true makes the design lint strict, scripts/design-lint/plugin.mjs)
